newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine inflation seen low despite oil prices.
newsitem.headline: Philippine inflation seen low despite oil prices.

text.p: Philippine Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo said on Monday inflation rate will remain within the six to seven percent range for the year despite the oil price increase announced late last week.
"If it's going to have an effect on inflation, it will be minimal so that we can still atain an average of six to seven percent this year," de Ocampo told reporters.
The inflation rate averaged 4.6 percent in the first six months of the year.
Oil companies raised their prices effective August 1 following the sharp depreciation of the peso against the dollar. Most of the country's petroleum products are imported.
De Ocampo said the new price schedule should not hurt the lower-income consumers since the biggest increases have been in high-end petroleum products.
